new_statements.quote: All NLori dialects use the stressed suffixes -ō(n) for animates, -yā for inanimates [...] All Lori dialects possess (1) the eżāfa, unstressed lax -e [...] (2) the relative marker (Ḵor, Gi, Ča, BGr unstressed -Ī [...] and (4) the definite object marker (in all dialects unstressed -ne/-na [...]. Verbal constructions are based on three stems, present, past, and perfect. The final syllable of the past and perfect stems is stressed. Presents are stressed on the personal ending except when negated or in the subjunctive mood, in which case stress shifts to the prefix. [...] The past tense is built on a past stem plus personal suffixes, the same as the present tense suffixes, though unstressed, except for third singular, which is unmarked.

The final syllable of the past and perfect stems is stressed. Presents are stressed on the personal ending except when negated or…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No explicit general rule is stated; the morphological facts given amount to a Persian-type system: stress falls on the last syllable of the word including stressed suffixes (plural -ō(n)/-yā, past and perfect stems stressed on their final syllable, present-tense personal endings stressed), while enclitics (eżāfa, relative/indefinite -Ī, object marker -ne/-na, past-tense personal endings) are unstressed; the negative prefix na- and the subjunctive/imperative prefix ba- take the stress away from the stem/ending. The demarcative suffix -(e)ka is equated with Tehrani Persian stressed final -é, and the Ḵorramābādi deictive suffix -a is stressed.
new_statements.exceptions: Negated and subjunctive present forms and imperatives are stressed on the prefix (ba-, na-); past-tense personal endings and the clitic markers (eżāfa, relative, indefinite, object marker) are unstressed; 'both with stress on the final syllable' is stated for the stative-perfect forms Ḵor nešessā́-m, Dez versī́d-am, Šuš versā́d-am.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (morphological word plus suffixes/prefixes); statements cover Northern Lori generally (Ḵorramābādi, Giōni, Čagani, Bālā Gerivāʾi) and some hold for all Lori dialects; no phrase-level or citation-form discussion.
new_statements.identity_note: The MacKinnon Iranica article describes 'Northern Lori' (NLori) as a group: Ḵorramābādi (Khorramabad city), Giōni, Čagani and Bālā Gerivāʾi, all under Glottolog nort2645 (lrc); some stress statements are made for 'all Lori dialects' and therefore also cover Southern Luri/Bakhtiari (bakh1245, sout2647), which are separate catalog entries. Mann 1904 groups Feili (= Northern Luri) with Mamasani and Bakhtiari.

sources.locator: Section MORPHOLOGY, subsections 'Nominal Morphology. Noun' and 'Verb Morphology. Verb' (unpaginated online article)
sources.note: No stress paragraph in the PHONOLOGY section; in MORPHOLOGY it states that NLori plural suffixes -ō(n)/-yā are stressed, the eżāfa, relative/indefinite marker and object marker are unstressed, the demarcative suffix corresponds to Persian stressed final -é, past and perfect stems are stressed on their final syllable, presents are stressed on the personal ending except negated/subjunctive forms where stress shifts to the prefix (stressed ba-, na-), and past-tense personal endings are unstressed.
